description: No-op / padding token -- 4 bytes, no operands. Its dispatch slot is the shared return-0 stub, so it does nothing at runtime. Shipped cutscenes emit it inertly between statements (interspersed padding / alignment). Harmless to keep or delete.
Copies bit 0 of arg into bit 3 (0x8) of the scene ctx's control field at +120. `ctx[+120] = (ctx[+120] & ~8) | ((arg & 1) << 3)`. Author use unknown; likely a scene mode flag toggle.

WAIT — pause the scene for a scripted duration. The one argument is a TIME in script units: 200 units = 1 frame, so 12000 = 1 second, 6000 = 0.5 s, 3000 = 0.25 s (the corpus's four most common values are exactly these). Any value 1..200 yields exactly one frame — `Wait(1)` is the idiomatic single-frame yield. This is the single most common pacing op (5,529 uses). Two traps, both engine-verified: the argument's expression KIND must be 0 (a computed expression — a plain literal is silently ignored, which is why the compiler always emits waits as expressions), and there must be EXACTLY one argument. IDA-verified as the wait primitive (vm[+120] = units, state -> WAITING; RF4S.exe+0x1FAB50).

End the current quest-reaction beat and wait: signals the scene controller idle (sceneCtx+872->child[+24][+116] = 1, the same write EndDialogue does), advances the quest-reaction dispatch state (Quest_OnReactionDispatched_AdvanceState), then - if the script task is in run-state 4 - writes arg0 into the task's wait field (+120, state 4->2), i.e. the same duration mechanism as Wait. Same units as Wait (200 = 1 frame); retail passes durations like 1 (minimal yield) or 6000 (30 frames). 267 retail uses, always 1 arg.

Redirect the VM to a target pc when the scene is in the pending-reaction state (ctx state 4) — a lightweight conditional jump used inside quest-reaction sequences (does not advance any quest state). arg0 = target.

Show an NPC speech/thought bubble — a variant form of ShowNpcBubble (op 6) built on the same NpcBubble_DispatchFromDescriptor pipeline. Blocks (returns busy) until any active screen fade completes. Takes THREE args (corpus: all 793 uses pass 3): arg0 = line id (into rf3mc.<locale>; descriptor u16 slot 0), arg1 = sub-token (descriptor u16 slot 1), arg2 = a byte param/emote (descriptor byte 6; corpus values like 254). The old hint list promised a 4th sfx/emote arg that the handler never reads.

prototype: ShowNpcBubble(content id, sub, param, sfx/emote id)
description: Show an NPC speech/thought bubble — the core bubble op. arg0 = content id with a dispatch: < 1000 = builtin EMOTE (emote-to-string table); 1000..1927 = dialogue STRING, index = id - 1000 (out of range clamps to 1000; 928 valid entries). arg1 = sub-token, arg2 = extra param (PSB-emote capable), arg3 = sfx/emote (>= 0x1F0 plays a voice line via the NPC-variant remap, else an emote id). Blocks until any active screen fade completes; re-showing identical text is a no-op (per-slot last-text cache).

prototype: ShowNpcBubble(content id, sub, param, sfx/emote id)
description: Alias of op 6 (same handler): show an NPC speech/thought bubble.

Show a dialogue line. arg0 = line id: >=0x30 = text-archive entry id (the common case, rendered as DIALOG #NNNN), 1-26 = standard slot load, 27-47 = event-participant line (portrait shown for 27-33/41-47), 0xFFFF = end marker. Also picks the speaker's dialogue tick-chime SFX class (Dialogue_PickChimeClassForSpeaker) before showing the text. SPEAKER NOTE (IDA-verified 2026-09-25): arg0 is a NAME-ARCHIVE id, not a text line -- the handler loads that name into the name plate of the message box (Dialogue_LoadAndShowText with the name archive of the task, the same path as SetSpeakerVoice), so the following DIALOG lines are spoken by it. Dialogue_ProcessLineDirective RF4S.exe+0x209DF0: 1-26 = the name of that villager (1 = Vishnal), >= 48 = any name entry, 0 = clear the name, 27-47 = an event participant resolved at run time.
Show a dialogue line (portrait speaks; reads speaker/line tokens).

Set the speaker for the following DIALOG line(s) to a NAMED VOICE: name plate only, NO portrait ('no portrait dispatch' — the handler's own contract). This is how off-screen and un-introduced characters speak — the opening's captain monologue (name string 738) and the stowaway bandits' whispers (392) both talk through it. arg0 = the NAME-PLATE string id: an entry of the character-name archive (the same list as char_names.json -- 21 Ventuswill, 236 Ethelwill, 392 '???', 738 Joyful Captain; not an rf3mc line id), shown through Dialogue_LoadAndShowText(archive, id, 2) and latched at task+108 so repeating it is free. arg1 = the TEXT BLIP, the tick sound played while the line types out (Dialogue_SetTickChimeSfxId; no voice acting is involved; the typewriter, Sprite_TickTypewriterDripText RF4S.exe+0x246AD0, plays it on every 4th character and restarts the count at each line break): 0 = male blip (sfx 16785916 = SE_WORDS_M.wav), 1 = female blip (16785917 = SE_WORDS_F.ogg), 2 = monster / animal blip (16785918 = SE_WORDS_O.wav; Buffamoo, Fiergaenger), 3 = dragon blip (16785975 = SE_WORDS_D.wav; Ventuswill in dragon form, Ancient Bone) -- names from common_audio_data.bdat, the files sit in bundleMain; 4+ = the PLAYER's own blip -- male for Lest's model (model 1217 = NPC_PLAYER_00), female for Frey's (1233 = NPC_PLAYER_01), male again when neither and player control flag 0x8000000 is set. Shipped uses: 651x 0, 170x 1, 5x 2, 105x 3 (931 in all). IDA-verified (NpcBubble_DispatchSimpleScriptedLine, RF4S.exe+0x20A240).

Name-label toggle for the following lines: writes bit 0 of the dialogue flags word (g_gameGlobalsSlotTable.entries[4]) = (arg == 0) (ScriptVMOp11_SetSceneStateBit0FromArg). Dialogue_LoadAndShowLine / Dialogue_LoadAndShowText / DialogueBox_SpawnBubbleAndSpeakerNameSprites copy that bit into the speaker-name label's hide bit (sprite flag 8) -- the same bit narration mode and the '???' no-name entry force on. So 0 = hide the name (inner voice, sound words, retold speech), 1 = show it. It does NOT pick a side: the left/right slot comes from the portrait cue (SetSpeakerX left/right). Loading a new name plate (SetSpeakerVoice / DialogueLine) clears the bit again. Corpus: bank 300 alternates 1 before quoted speech and 0 before first-person narration; bank 4 puts 0 before '*WHOOSH!*' (IDA + corpus 2026-09-25).
Show a scripted speech bubble (3 tokens: speaker, index, sub).

prototype: ShowSpeakerBubble(speaker, line index, sub, sfx/emote id)
description: Show a speech bubble line for a SPEAKER, with emote-PSB support. arg0 = speaker (npc/char id: selects the chime class, name text and per-NPC emote byte; with save-config emote flag 0x40 set, ids >= 30 index g_npcEmotePsbTable and get substituted -- the Switch-era PSB emote path). arg1 = line index (passed to Dialogue_LoadAndShowText). arg2 = sub/param. arg3 = trigger: >= 0x1F0 plays a voice sfx, else stored as the bubble emote byte.

Unbound opcode -- the dispatch slot points at the table's default filler (no real handler), so the game's scripts never emit it. Reserved / removed in the PC port.

Turn an actor toward a target facing. arg0 = actor (char id, 0=player; resolved by matching the scene's two bound actor slots ctx+88/ctx+96, not the global tables). arg1 = TARGET facing, written raw (u16) to motion field +94 while +92 snapshots the current facing (+44) as the lerp start; bit 0x8000 of arg1 clears motion byte +99 (turn-mode/snap selector, default 1). arg2 = TURN SPEED: run through the engine's canonical speed formula ((167773*x)>>12, here x25 scale) into motion field +88, with turn progress (+32) reset to 0. NOTE: the previous hints had arg1/arg2 swapped (rate vs angle).
Alias of op 77 (same handler): set an actor's target facing angle + turn rate.

Turn an actor by a RELATIVE amount: adds signed arg1 to the motion target-turn field (+94); arg1's sign also sets the turn-direction byte (+99: positive=1, negative=0 — the old 'bit 0x8000 = ease vs snap' claim was just this sign bit). arg2 = turn SPEED, not an angle: it goes through the same 167773/4096 (x40.96, then x25) Q12 speed conversion as the move ops' speed channel and lands in motion +88. arg0 = actor (char id, matched against the two scene actor slots; 0 = player). Corpus shows paired +40/-40 wiggles at speed 100 during dialogue (head-shake beats).
Alias of op 79 (same handler): add to an actor's turn rate + aim it at an angle.

1 while the actor is mid-motion — its motion-state code (motion+42 & 0x7C) is NOT the settled/idle value 0x10; 0 once settled. arg0 = actor (matched against the scene's two participant slots). Wait-for-move-done predicate.
Alias of op 81 (same handler): 1 while the actor is mid-motion, 0 when settled.

Close on-screen dialogue bubble(s) and BLOCK the scene until the close animation finishes. arg selects which: 0 = close the FIRST bubble slot (ctx+88), 1 = close the SECOND slot (ctx+96), any other value = close BOTH. Each path calls DialogueBubble_TransitionState(slot, 0) and then keeps returning 'blocked' while the bubble state / g_npcBubbleActiveByScreen shows a bubble still closing. Use before switching speakers or ending a conversation cleanly. (The old hint '0 = both' was wrong: 0 closes one slot; only a value other than 0/1 closes both.)

Low-level motion tuning: write a value to an actor's motion-struct field +62 (only if the 3rd arg is non-zero). arg0 = actor (matched vs the scene's participant slots), arg1 = value, arg2 = apply flag. Engine-internal motion parameter — rarely needed directly.
Low-level motion tuning: write a value to an actor's motion-struct field +56. arg0 = actor, arg1 = value. Engine-internal motion parameter.
Alias of op 85 (same handler): write actor motion field +56.
Low-level motion tuning: write a value to an actor's motion-struct field +60. arg0 = actor, arg1 = value. Engine-internal motion parameter.
Alias of op 87 (same handler): write actor motion field +60.

Low-level motion tuning: writes a per-actor motion mask byte (actor motion struct +66). arg0 = actor (matched against the scene's two participant slots at ctx+96/+88, like op 81). arg1 is a LEVEL, not a raw mask: the byte written is 127>>arg1; arg1 = 0 (or out of 1..254) writes 0xFF (all bits). Engine-internal; exact field semantics uncertain.

Alias of op 89 (same handler): set an actor's motion mask byte (motion struct +66) from a SHIFT COUNT, not a raw mask: writes 127>>n for n in 1..254, otherwise 0xFF. arg0 = actor (char id, resolved via a1+96/+88). Exact field semantics uncertain; unused in the shipped corpus.
Set or clear bit [arg0] of the scene's local bit-field (scene context +404): arg1 non-zero sets the bit, zero clears it. Scene-local scratch flags for a scene script's own bookkeeping.

Close both speaker bubbles and commit the dialogue state -- the end of a spoken exchange. ALSO CLEARS THE SPEAKER (sceneCtx+108 = -1): the next DIALOG without a new SetSpeaker is narration again (plain box, no name/portrait). Returns to the scene controller when no other event is in flight. The #2 most-used action op (10,564 uses) -- every dialogue beat ends with one.

Set the dialogue box style from an argument (the general form of ops 94-97, and the only way to get style 4). It sets the MESSAGE-BOX STYLE, not a face (verified 2026-09-25: Dialogue_SetSpeakerEmoteAndRetargetPortrait RF4S.exe+0x234E20 stores it at dialogue task +160; Dialogue_RetargetPortraitAndBubble +0x2380B0 then shows window art talk_win<n> (archive 15851+n) and tail talk_hige<n> (15846+n); Dialogue_SetTimingState +0x238350 adds the effect). 0 = normal box, 1 = shout (jagged box; everything shakes for 10 frames and the screen flashes), 2 = thought (cloud box with a bubble-trail tail; the box floats for ~1 s -- it does not delay the line), 3 = trembling (wavy box; a 10-frame sideways shake), 4 = tail only (no box). 5-7 would read unrelated textures.
